title: Henri IV to Philippe de Bethune (Rome), 9, 10 and 22 Nov 1601, BnF fr. 3484 nos. 7, 8, 12

plaintext.source: The minute in clear, f. 36r-v (item 9, 'copie du n. precedent')

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, 2000 and 3996 px, crops at 1.5x-4x
transcription.notes: About 480 symbols in four blocks per NOTES; corpus_v2.txt pairs them with plaintext, so not measured.

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaf; a clear copy may be in Cinq cents de Colbert 346 or Halphen's edition, neither consulted.

transcription.notes: Counted by a scratch script over the token field (the --measure line mode also counts the line labels and bars: 992/63). Three glyph families (g, m, r variants) are not separable at the available resolution; the transcription caps decoding at about 71 % of letters.
80 cipher runs; counted by a scratch script over the token field (the file has label columns).

system.summary: Villeroy-office cipher: letters as figures and letter-shaped symbols with homophones, marked letters (comma, one or two dots) for words in alphabetical series, two-digit figures for names and syllables.

diacritics.note: Comma, one dot or two dots on a letter select a word series (f, = le; x, = que; t: = de).

system.doubled_letters: special sign (phi doubles the preceding symbol)
system.sibling_key: Bazeries 1901 prints the 1599 key given to Bethune's brother, same office and design, other values; used for the design only.
system.notes: Known names: 48 Cardinal, 17 Aldobrandin, 7 le Roy d'Espagne; 61 qui, 63 re, 65 si, 68 tout, 71 tion, 73 vostre. 72 = vous proposed, unconfirmed.

prior_solution.where: Clear minute of the 10 Nov letter (f. 36) and marginal glosses of other letters in the same volume; none for 9 or 22 Nov

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: EM alignment of cipher and minute (em_align.py)
oracle ceiling and control harness (oracle.py, eval.py)

solution.what: Volume fetched from Gallica; leaves mapped; the clear minute of 10 Nov found at f. 36 by reading the sheets.
EM alignment of the 10 Nov cipher with its minute plus the glossed passages of 8 Nov and 10 Dec gives the letter values and word signs.
10 Nov letter read in full against the minute.
9 Nov letter decoded with the key and language-model decoders: about six words in ten.
4x re-transcription fixed the doubling sign and the syllable groups 61-73.
Oracle on the known-plaintext blocks: transcription caps decoding at about 71 % of letters; decoder already at the ceiling.
Automatic glyph segmentation and template alignment.
22 Nov letter transcribed in full; clear text read, cipher runs decode to fragments only.
Full-resolution re-reading and figure-split lattice on f. 33; union of two independent readings worth about 2.9 points.
Xivrey, Melanges de Colbert 17, fr. 3677/3678 excluded; Cinq cents de Colbert 346 and Halphen's edition identified, not accessible.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by EM alignment of the 10 Nov 1601 cipher (f. 34) with its clear minute four leaves on (f. 36) and the marginal glosses of the 8 Nov and 10 Dec letters in the same volume (BnF fr. 3484), then applied to the unglossed 9 and 22 Nov letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: NOTES prose, not measured: no token-level reading file exists for the 9 Nov (decode_f33_v3.txt is decoder output over a ~70%-accurate glyph transcription, with no ground truth) or 22 Nov letters (reading_22nov.md gives substance only); the 10 Nov passages are read from the clear minute (reading_10nov.md). The decoder's measured accuracy on known text is 74.5% letters / 51.8% words (eval.py).
outcome.notes: 10 Nov read in full; 9 Nov about six words in ten; 22 Nov clear text read, cipher in fragments. Open code groups include 44, 45, 62, 66-72, 26-28, 5, 3, 8. fraction_read estimated from the notes (10 Nov full; 9 Nov about half the words; 22 Nov clear text read, cipher runs fragments only), not measured. codes_open counts the 19 code numbers listed open in NOTES (2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 12, 20, 26-28, 31, 44, 45, 62, 66, 67, 69, 72, 80); total not counted.

gaps.item: 9 Nov 1601 letter, f. 33 (about half the words)
gaps.detail: third pass measured the ceiling as set by the glyph transcription (similar glyphs differ by a hook), not by the key
decode2.py gives fragments only, the same transcription ceiling
glossed leaves ff. 49v-50r, 53r, 56r carry verbatim decipherments containing 66 and 72, but the eight cipher lines of f. 53r were never transcribed/aligned

gaps.item: clear copies in BnF Cinq cents de Colbert 346
gaps.detail: copy register 23 Aug 1601 - 22 Nov 1602, not digitised (Gallica SRU no record)
